Commentary.Commentary: MOHAMMAD AMIR TO START THE PROCEEDINGS FOR PAKISTAN!
The Pakistani players are out in the middle. The English openers Alex Hales and Alastair Cook walk into the middle.
Day 3, Session 3

A brilliant batting performance from Pakistan led by the mighty Younis who shut his critics' mouth with an epic double ton. Asad Shafiq's ton yesterday was a vital one too as his stand of 150 with Younis virtually set it up for the tourists. Woakes and Finn were the major wicket takers for England with three apiece but it was a long toil for the hosts' bowlers. With a big deficit of 214, England have a tough task in hand. Join us in a while for the final session of the day.

This session - 29 overs, 125 runs, 3 wickets. Tremendous couple of hours for Pakistan after lunch. Younis Khan converted his century into a double ton and added a brisk 97-run stand for the ninth wicket with Amir. The southpaw hung in well and gave good support to Younis as the pair ensured that the visitors' first innings lead was substantial. Younis fell with 10 minutes left to tea but Amir played a few shots to get the lead past the 210-run mark.

England's bowlers barring Woakes weren't quite on the money. Consistency was missing although credit must be given to Younis and Sarfraz with the latter in particular using his fancy footwork to upset the bowlers' rhythm. Woakes looked like the only bowler to get a wicket and he ended up breaking the partnership. Apart from that success, there wasn't much joy for the hosts in the morning. They will want to come back after the break and wrap up the innings quickly. Tune in for the second session in a while.

This session - 26 overs, 77 runs, 1 wicket. Another solid session for Pakistan as they continued to steadily build on their first innings lead which is now 89. Younis and Sarfraz negotiated the first hour with ease and their 77-run stand was pivotal for the tourists in the probing morning session. Although Sarfraz fell after yet another start, Younis continued to dominate and is nearing to another 150-plus score in Tests. He has the tail for company and will hope to eke out as much lead as possible for Pakistan.

Will Younis stand as a wall and take the game away from the English side or will the home side display their uninhibited style of play and come back big time in the match? Join us for the Third Day of the final Test Match which promises to be an enticing day of cricket.

What more could we have asked for? The English seamers bending their back and the Pakistani top and middle order putting up a valiant show made for a thrilling second day of the final Test. Asad Shafiq's classy century and Younis Khan's resolute ton proved to be the icing on the cake! Pakistan are well poised at the moment and would like to stretch their lead above the 100-150 run mark while England would like to break the crucial partnership between Younis Khan and Sarfaraz Ahmed and pave a way to come back in the match.

The tourists are ahead but only slightly. As the Edgbaston Test showed, a big first innings lead doesn't necessarily guarantee a win and Pakistan will want to stretch it as much as possible. Credit should be given to Younis and Shafiq for getting stuck in.
